rule: Pairs come from legal.json related_events only: each event is paired with the earliest later legal item that lists it. Chronology, not causation.

pairs.text: Starfish Prime (1962), then the Limited Test Ban Treaty (1963), which followed it
North Korean GNSS jamming (from 2010), then an ICAO Assembly finding on GNSS interference (2025), which SWF also ties to the Baltic case
Shakti destructive test (2019), then UNGA 77/41 (2022), a non-binding call not to conduct destructive DA-ASAT tests
Cosmos 1408 destructive test (2021), then a US test moratorium (2022, unilateral pledge)
Baltic-region GNSS interference (from 2023), then an ICAO Assembly finding on recurring GNSS interference (2025)
Jamming of European satellites (2024), then ITU RRB “grave concern” (2024)

open.text: Laser fired at a satellite (1997): no legal item in the ledger is related to it
open.basis: No related_events link; the ring states an absence in this ledger, not a finding that no rule exists.

open.text: Viasat cyberattack (2022): the only related legal item, Tallinn Manual 2.0 (2017), is soft law and pre-dates it
open.basis: tallinn-2017 lists ru-2022-viasat in related_events but is earlier, so it forms no forward pair.

dropped.reason: No sourced link: SWF and the treaty text do not connect the 1959 Bold Orion flyby to the Outer Space Treaty.
No sourced link: unga-77-41 relates to Cosmos 1408 and Shakti; a Fengyun-1C link would be the builder's inference.
